transcript:
Live from NPR News, I'm Lakshmi Singh.
A federal court hearing takes place later this hour over a lawsuit that CNN, MS Now
and Politico filed against the Trump administration after the president banned them, citing their
unfavorable coverage of him.
The Department of Justice now says these news outlets pose a security risk.
Ukrainian President Vladimir Zelensky has just addressed the UN General Assembly for
the fourth time since his country was invaded by Russia in 2022.
He calls Vladimir Putin's war "ridiculous."
I read President Trump's post on truth social.
The president wrote that Russia has lost control of its diesel oil industry due to its war
with Ukraine.
President Trump has blamed Ukraine's attacks on Russia's refineries for the surge in diesel
prices in the US.
A new poll finds voters continue to have a sour view of the president and Republicans
in general, as NPR's Stephen Fowler reports.
Those surveyed say they'd back Democrats for Congress by 12-point margin.
The latest NPR/PBS News mayorist poll shows deep dissatisfaction with President Trump
and the Republican Party.
Republicans have also lost their advantage on several key issues in the eyes of voters,
like gas prices, the economy, foreign policy, even immigration.
The poll also suggests Democrats have a notable edge in voter enthusiasm and support from
independents as a building wave of backlash to the party in power comes into focus.
These voters say they're more likely to pick a Democratic congressional candidate, 53-41%.
That swing from Trump's narrow popular vote victory in 2024 shows why reliably red states
like Ohio, Texas, and Iowa now have competitive House and Senate races.
Stephen Fowler, NPR News.
Chinese leader Xi Jinping is en route to the US.
President Trump will personally greet him at Joint Base Andrews later today.
NPR's Emily Fang reports a pageantry the White House is planning for the Chinese president.
The US military will conduct a flyover at the White House shortly before Trump meets
the Chinese leader on the Tarmac tonight, showing just how important Trump sees this
visit.
On Thursday, the Marine Band will welcome the Chinese leader with the anthems of both
countries and a state visit reception with hundreds of US military personnel and a gun
salute as well as another flyover with fighter planes.
In addition to the pomp, the two leaders are expected to talk about trade, the war on Iran,
and artificial intelligence.
Activists also want Trump to raise the issue of detained Americans and dissidents in China.
And then Trump and Xi will gather for a state dinner, paired back in part due to Trump's
East Wing construction project.
Emily Fang, NPR News, the White House.
Forecasters are tracking a Pacific cyclone described as one of the strongest in decades.
Hurricane Polo is expected to skirt Mexico's southwestern coast.
Meanwhile, another storm, Odales, had strengthened from a tropical storm to a hurricane over
that was far from land.
From Washington, it's NPR News.
In New York, Harvey Weinstein has been sentenced to 15 years in prison and Pierre's Chloe Weiner
has details.
Harvey Weinstein was first convicted of sex crimes in New York in 2020 and sentenced to
23 years in prison, but that was thrown out.
Prosecutors have since brought him back to court multiple times.
Last year, Weinstein was found guilty of sexually assaulting Miriam Haley in 2006, when she
was a production assistant.
The 15-year sentence is from that conviction.
Weinstein was found not guilty on another charge and two separate juries in New York
have been unable to reach a verdict on a charge of rape.
He was, however, convicted of rape in California in 2022.
He was sentenced to 16 years, but a court ruled earlier this year that he will need to
be re-sentenced.
Weinstein is now 74 years old and has numerous health problems.
Authorities pleaded not guilty to all charges.
Chloe Weiner, NPR News, New York.
After signing the pandemic agreement over a year ago, countries still are trying to
finalize part of the deal.
Here's NPR's Jonathan Lambert.
Countries are largely stuck on a key part of the pandemic agreement, how to share data
on pathogens and how to share the vaccines and drugs that get made from that data.
Wealthier countries want data on some new emerging virus to be as readily available
as possible to help companies develop vaccines as fast as possible.
Lower-income countries think that kind of system will repeat the same inequities of
the COVID-19 pandemic, where rich countries got vaccines way before lower-income countries.
So lower-income countries want to attach strings, trading access to the data for concessions
on vaccine sharing.
But countries are struggling to agree on how this would work.
Negotiations will continue on and off through May of 2027.
Jonathan Lambert, NPR News.
I'm Lakshmi Singh, NPR News, in Washington.

Ukrainian President Zelensky addresses UN General Assembly for fourth time since Russian invasion, calls Putin's war ridiculous

NPR/PBS News poll shows voters favor Democrats for Congress by 12-point margin over Republicans
Chinese leader Xi Jinping en route to US for state visit, Trump to greet him at Joint Base Andrews
Hurricane Polo tracked as one of strongest Pacific cyclones in decades, expected to skirt Mexico's southwestern coast
Harvey Weinstein sentenced to 15 years in prison in New York for sexual assault conviction
